'''Selman Akbulut''' (born 1949) is a [[Turkish people|Turkish]] [[mathematician]], specializing in research in [[topology]], and [[geometry]]. He was a professor at [[Michigan State University]] until February 2020.

==Career==
In 1975, he earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a student of [[Robion Kirby]]. In topology, he has worked on [[handlebody]] theory, low-dimensional [[manifold]]s,<ref name="4-manifolds">{{cite book |last1=Akbulut |first1=Selman |title=4-manifolds |date=2016 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780198784869 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1xMBDQAAQBAJ |accessdate=13 August 2019 |language=en}}</ref> [[symplectic topology]], [[G2 manifold]]s. In the topology of [[real algebraic set|real-algebraic set]]s, he and Henry C. King proved that every [[compact space|compact]] [[piecewise-linear manifold]] is a real-algebraic set; they discovered new topological invariants of real-algebraic sets.<ref>S. Akbulut and H.C. King, ''Topology of real algebraic sets'',  MSRI Publications, 25. Springer-Verlag, New York (1992) {{isbn|0-387-97744-9}}</ref>

He was a visiting scholar several times at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] (in 1975-76, 1980–81, 2002, and 2005).<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=1 Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106144307/http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=1 |date=2013-01-06 }}</ref>

On February 14, 2020, Akbulut was removed from his tenured position at MSU by the Board of Trustees, after disputes over his teaching allotments and communications with colleagues.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Graham |first1=Karly |last2=Monroe |first2=Maddie |title=Board of Trustees fires tenured professor for cause |url=https://statenews.com/article/2020/02/board-of-trustees-fires-tenured-professor-for-cause?ct=content_open&cv=cbox_latest |work=The State News |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name="Dismissal">{{cite web |last1=Stanley |first1=Samuel L. |title=Dismissal of Tenured Faculty for Cause |url=https://trustees.msu.edu/meetings/AA2-Dismissal%20of%20Tenured%20Facutly%20for%20Cause1.pdf |website=MSU Board of Trustees |accessdate=14 February 2020 |archive-date=15 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200215023939/https://trustees.msu.edu/meetings/AA2-Dismissal%20of%20Tenured%20Facutly%20for%20Cause1.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="WWMT">{{cite news |last1=Frost |first1=Mikenzie |title=MSU Trustees dismiss tenured professor, address Title IX investigation delays |url=https://wwmt.com/news/state/msu-trustees-dismiss-tenured-professor-address-title-ix-investigation-delays |accessdate=14 February 2020 |work=WWMT |date=14 February 2020}}</ref>

==Contributions==
He has developed 4-dimensional handlebody techniques, settling conjectures and solving problems about 4-manifolds, such as a conjecture of [[Christopher Zeeman]],<ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S. | title=A solution to a conjecture of Zeeman | journal=Topology | volume=30 | issue=3 | date=1991 | doi=10.1016/0040-9383(91)90028-3 | pages=513–515 | url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0040938391900283 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> the [[Dolgachev surface|Harer&ndash;Kas&ndash;Kirby conjecture]], a problem of [[Martin Scharlemann]],<ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S.| title=Scharlemann's Manifold is Standard | journal=The Annals of Mathematics | volume=149 | issue=2 | date=1999 | doi=10.2307/120972 | doi-access=free | pages=497–510 | jstor=120972| arxiv=math/9712255 }}</ref> and problems of [[Sylvain Cappell]] and [[Julius Shaneson]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S. | title=Cappell-Shaneson homotopy spheres are standard | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=171 | issue=3 | date=2010 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2010.171.2171 | doi-access=free | pages=2171–2175 | url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v171-n3-p18-p.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S. | title=Cappell–Shaneson's 4–dimensional s –cobordism | journal=Geometry & Topology | volume=6 | issue=1 | date=2002 | issn=1364-0380 | doi=10.2140/gt.2002.6.425 | doi-access=free | pages=425–494 | url=http://msp.org/gt/2002/6-1/gt-v6-n1-p16-p.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Freedman | first1=M.H. | last2=Gompf | first2=R.E. | last3=Morrison | first3=S. | last4=Walker | first4=K. | title=Man and machine thinking about the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture | journal=Quantum Topology | volume=1 | issue=2 | date=2010-06-22 | issn=1663-487X | doi=10.4171/qt/5 | doi-access=free | pages=171–208 | url=https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/36744 | arxiv=0906.5177 }}</ref>
He constructed an exotic compact 4-manifold (with boundary) from which he discovered "[[Akbulut cork]]s".<ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S. | title=A fake compact contractible 4-manifold | journal=[[Journal of Differential Geometry]] | volume=33 | issue=2 | date=1991-01-01 | issn=0022-040X | doi=10.4310/jdg/1214446320 | doi-access=free | url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-differential-geometry/volume-33/issue-2/A-fake-compact-contractible-4-manifold/10.4310/jdg/1214446320.pdf | pages=335–356}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Akbulut | first=S. | title=An exotic 4-manifold | journal=Journal of Differential Geometry | volume=33 | issue=2 | date=1991-01-01 | issn=0022-040X | doi=10.4310/jdg/1214446321 | doi-access=free | pages=357–361}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Ozbagci | first1=B. | last2=Stipsicz | first2=A.I. | title=Surgery on Contact 3-Manifolds and Stein Surfaces | publisher=Springer Science & Business Media | publication-place=Berlin | date=2004 | isbn=978-3-540-22944-5 | page=14}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last=Scorpan | first=A. | title=The Wild World of 4-Manifolds | publisher=American Mathematical Soc. | publication-place=Providence, RI | date=2005 | isbn=0-8218-3749-4 | page=90}}</ref> 

His most recent results concern the  4-dimensional [[Smooth manifold|smooth]] [[Poincaré conjecture]].<ref name="Secret">{{cite web |last1=Morrison |first1=Scott |title=Mike Freedman on SPC4 |url=http://sbseminar.wordpress.com/category/low-dimensional-topology/poincare-conjecture/ |website=Secret Blogging Seminar |date=19 April 2011 |accessdate=13 August 2019 |language=en}}</ref>  He has supervised 14 Ph.D. students as of 2019. He has more than 100 papers and three books published, and several books edited.
